cohorts.subjects: Living ambulatory adult patients having abdominopelvic CT at the authors' institution (Prince of Wales Hospital, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China), measured prospectively between Feb 2014 and Jan 2015. Over 99% of the patient population was ethnically Chinese; patients with non-Chinese names were not included. Excluded: skeletal disorders such as dwarfism or scoliosis (printed 'skeletal orders'), prior lumbar surgery, a childhood chronic inflammatory condition, and a major lumbar morphological abnormality such as vertebral fracture or dysraphism. Recruited by quota, 90 of each sex in each 10-year age band (20-29, 30-39 etc.), each band closed at 90. Table S5 regroups them into 21-40, 41-60 and 61-80 years (180 per sex each); Table 7 compares the largest and smallest 25% at each level and sex, matched for height (group sizes not printed). Not healthy volunteers: the authors argue canal development ends by 17 years.
cohorts.n_units: 5,400 lumbar levels (L1 to L5, mid-pedicle) of 1,080 patients

cohorts.subjects: 20 randomly selected subjects, five levels each (L1 to L5), measured twice by one reader with the computerized method 1 week apart, blinded to the first result, and once manually by a second reader. Inference: drawn from the 1,080 patients; the paper does not say from which pool, nor their sex or age.

techniques.instrument: 64-slice multidetector CT (LightSpeed VCT, GE Healthcare), reconstructive resolution 0.6 mm, bone window; semi-automated computerized segmentation software (not named; the vertebral body method cites Yushkevich 2006, ref 8); SPSS 22 for statistics
techniques.how: For each of L1 to L5 the volume is reoriented to give a plane at right angles to the vertebral body and the mid-pedicle axial image is found automatically, orthogonal to the mid-sagittal plane. On that one image: osseous canal CSA by seed-growing segmentation after rigid co-registration, then manual correction of the canal boundary; canal depth from the posterior margin of the body to the cortex of the neural arch at the base of the spinous process; canal width between the inner margins of the two pedicles; vertebral body CSA by an attenuation threshold against the surrounding soft tissue, then manual correction with the pedicle bases demarcated; and the canal CSA / body CSA ratio. Smallest-25% cut-offs from per-sex histograms (Figures S1-S3).
techniques.magnification: not applicable: measured on reformatted CT images; no calibration described
techniques.observers: one operator for all analysis; the same reader repeated the reliability subset 1 week apart

techniques.how: A second reader independently selected the image and manually measured canal CSA, depth and width at L1 to L5 on the same 20 subjects; compared with the second computerized reading by intraclass correlation, reported per level only. Inference: on the same CT data.
Height (cm) and weight (kg) of every patient recorded before the CT examination; BMI derived.

within_paper: One set of subjects throughout: every table and figure (Tables 1-7, S1-S6, Figures S1-S3) is of the same 1,080 patients, N = 540 per sex, p. 672 (PDF 2) and suppl. (PDF 10-14). Table S5's age groups (180 per sex each) and Table 7's largest and smallest quartile groups are subsets of them, as are the adjusted means of Tables S1-S4 and S6, which re-express the same measurements. The reliability study measured the same 20 subjects (100 levels) twice by the computerized method and once manually by a second reader, p. 673 (PDF 3); Inference: those 20 are drawn from the 1,080.
